meta.tagline: Measure every cryptographic path. With evidence, not assumption.

challenge.title: The challenge
challenge.headline: Quantum risk starts before the break. Most security stacks cannot see
challenge.body: Long-life data can be captured now, classical trust anchors can outlive migration plans, and cryptographic implementations can drift in ways an inventory will never show. The question is not only what algorithm is deployed.
challenge.bodyEmphasis: It is how the system behaves while you move.

cards.label: 01 CAPTURED NOW
cards.title: Stored today. Exposed later.
cards.body: Long-life encrypted data can be retained now and attacked once quantum capability becomes practical.

cards.label: 02 TRUST FROZEN IN PLACE
cards.title: Certificates become blockers.
cards.body: Long-lived identities, signing dependencies and trust anchors make migration harder than replacing one algorithm.

cards.label: 03 BEHAVIOUR NOT VISIBLE
cards.title: Crypto can pass and still drift.
cards.body: Timing, symmetry, parity and noise can reveal implementation-level exposure that configuration checks do not show.

challenge.stakes: data can outlive today's cryptography · migration dependencies sit across identity and applications · production is the wrong place to discover the gap.

solution.title: The solution
solution.eyebrow: The observation layer for post-quantum migration
solution.lead: Software beside your cryptographic stack, without decrypting the payload.
solution.sub: QSP compares classical and post-quantum paths under the same conditions and shows where exposure persists.
solution.subEmphasis: Controlled sandbox. Defined interfaces. No production data.

points.title: Exposure, per workload
points.body: Classical and PQC paths measured side by side.

points.title: Behavioural drift surfaced
points.body: Symmetry, timing, parity and noise tracked independently.

points.title: Trust without decryption
points.body: Runtime behaviour becomes a statistical trust state.

points.title: Lightweight integration
points.body: Config-file hooks. Structured JSON/CSV. No invasive changes.

differentiation.title: Differentiation
differentiation.eyebrow: Why this works, and why now

points.title: Behaviour, not checklist
points.lead: We measure what the session does.
points.body: Inventory is the evidence underneath it, not the conclusion.

points.title: Side by side, before rollout
points.body: Classical and post-quantum paths face the same test.

points.title: Payload stays closed
points.lead: Observe the behaviour. Not the content.
points.body: Key health, timing and protocol state stay measurable.

points.title: Fits the lab you have
points.body: Defined interfaces. No invasive rack changes.

differentiation.standing: QSP platform defined · controlled sandbox protocol · Qatar validation route identified · research-grade scorecards and JSON/CSV outputs

asks.title: The asks
asks.eyebrow: Where an introduction changes the outcome
asks.headline: Two doors in Qatar.

items.title: A quantum environment for a scoped validation
items.body: One controlled QKD/PQC environment. QSP beside it. Run the same sessions and compare the behaviour. If it shows nothing useful, we stop.

items.title: An enterprise security team for a controlled sandbox
items.body: One workload. Two isolated non-production environments: classical and post-quantum. No live data. Time-boxed, auditable, decision-ready output.

asks.note: Target organisations shown for introduction context; no partnership implied.
